parts.role: Runs the firmware and supplies 3.3 V from its USB-powered regulator.
Senses how bright the room is.
With the LDR, turns light level into a voltage the ESP32 can measure.
Limits the LED current to a level a GPIO pin can safely supply.
The lamp itself, at indicator brightness.

nets.name: +3V3
nets.why: One 3.3 V supply from the ESP32 board’s regulator. Every part here runs at 3.3 V, so its signals match the ESP32’s 3.3 V logic.

nets.name: GND
nets.why: Common ground. Every signal is measured against it, so every part must share it.

nets.name: LIGHT_SENSE
nets.why: The midpoint of a voltage divider. More light lowers the LDR’s resistance, so this voltage rises. GPIO34 is on ADC1, which keeps working while Wi-Fi is on; it is input-only, which is fine for reading.

nets.name: LED_DRIVE
nets.why: GPIO25 switches the LED on and off (or dims it with PWM) through the current-limiting resistor.

nets.name: LED_A
nets.why: Resistor to LED anode. Current ≈ (3.3 V − 2.0 V) ÷ 150 Ω ≈ 8.7 mA, below the ~20 mA a GPIO should supply. Check the forward voltage of your LED.

notes.text: Indicator-scale lamp: one LED straight from a GPIO pin. A brighter lamp needs a MOSFET driver and its own supply, which this preview does not design.
LDRs vary a lot. Calibrate the threshold in your own room.
